tracks.title: Wearable therapeutics
tracks.blurb: Wearables that work on the body's own processes without needing your attention, from pacing your breathing and vibrotactile therapy for spasticity to vagus nerve stimulation during meals and restoring facial expression.

tracks.title: Brain–computer interfaces
tracks.blurb: Passively learnable BCIs, how fast any interface can carry information, and teaching the BCI community.

tracks.title: Artificial intelligence
tracks.blurb: Systems that learn from human activity and support work, from weakly supervised visual learning to persistent AI agents.

tracks.title: Wearable sensing
tracks.blurb: Sensing force, motion and health on the body, and keeping that data with the person it describes.

tracks.title: Passive haptic learning
tracks.blurb: Learning motor skills such as piano through tactile cues, without active practice.

tracks.title: Subtle interaction
tracks.blurb: Hands-free, eyes-free input. Silent speech, tongue and gaze, fingerspelling.

tracks.title: Haptics
tracks.blurb: Touch and vibration for motor learning and rehabilitation, from passive piano rehearsal to vibrotactile stimulation for spasticity.

tracks.title: Wearables
tracks.blurb: Body-worn sensing, stimulation, and input systems, from smart rings and head-worn devices to haptic gloves and therapeutic wraps.

tracks.title: Human augmentation
tracks.blurb: Interfaces that extend or restore human abilities through new input methods, passive skill learning, and physiological intervention.

tracks.title: Neural stimulation
tracks.blurb: Peripheral electrical stimulation for physiological intervention, including vagus nerve stimulation during eating and facial muscle stimulation for symmetry.

tracks.title: Accessibility
tracks.blurb: Designing with and for people with disabilities, from silent speech and ASL to facial paralysis and safer kitchens.

tracks.title: Social computing
tracks.blurb: Studies of online communities in social VR and of how people judge public-health messages.

tracks.title: Machine learning & vision
tracks.blurb: Learning from video, stereo images and telescope time series.

tracks.title: Neuroscience
tracks.blurb: Localizing working memory with task fMRI, at Neuromatch Academy.

tracks.title: Robotics
tracks.blurb: Autonomous robots for humanitarian demining and competition, before switching to augmentation in undergrad.

series.title: Talking without sound
series.blurb: From a retainer that reads your tongue to tongue gestures on head-worn displays.

series.title: Learning without practice
series.blurb: Passive haptic learning, first for piano and then for rehabilitation.

series.title: How wearables engage physiology
series.blurb: A progression in how wearables engage physiology: guiding voluntary breathing, afferent neuromodulation, autonomic signaling, then restoring facial expression.

series.title: How fast can an interface talk?
series.blurb: Information transfer rate, from BrainBraille to a public atlas comparing interfaces.

items.title: Choose your own AI future
items.excerpt: An interactive essay about possible AI futures and how they change when human capabilities advance too. Follow a series of choices about AI, then compare illustrated worlds shaped by different distributions of capability, power, and agency.

items.title: Wearable Health Trackers and Privacy
items.excerpt: I originally wrote this for a past iteration of CS3001: Computing and Society at Georgia Tech. I quite like it, and I think the issues are increasingly relevant, so I decided to put it up here. In 2014, Time Magazine crowned the Apple Watch as one of its "25 Best Inventions of the Year" (Time, 2014)

items.title: Artificial Intelligence through Symbiosis
items.excerpt: We investigated whether the structure of warehouse order-picking tasks could provide weak supervision for object recognition from egocentric video. The system learned visual object models from repeated picks without frame-level labels and was evaluated on independent orders.

items.title: Assistive Smart Stove for Safer Kitchens
items.excerpt: This coursework prototype combined mobile controls, burner reminders, an adjustable cooking surface, and a side-loading oven to explore support for memory, reach, and posture in the kitchen. A four-person Wizard-of-Oz study identified useful interactions and substantial usability issues, but did not include the intended older-adult population.

items.title: BCIhub: A Tutorial Repository by the BCI Society
items.excerpt: As part of the BCI Society's Postdoc & Student Committee, I helped develop tutorials for the BCI Meeting and began organizing the material in a reusable repository. The initial machine-learning notebook exposes the choices behind preprocessing, features, models, and evaluation rather than presenting only a final classifier score.

items.title: BionicFace: Closed-Loop Facial Muscle Stimulation for Facial Symmetry after Facial Paralysis
items.excerpt: BionicFace is an assistive wearable research project for people with chronic facial paralysis caused by nerve damage. We are exploring glasses-based facial sensing and closed-loop electrical muscle stimulation to support real-time upper-face symmetry during social expression and communication, with a focus on hardware integration, calibration, comfort, safety, and everyday use.

items.title: BrainBraille: A Passively Learnable Brain Computer Interface using fNIRS
items.excerpt: BrainBraille is an attempted-movement brain-computer interface that maps combinations of body regions to language. For my undergraduate thesis, I explored a wearable fNIRS implementation and examined whether transitions between movements could expand the command set while improving classification accuracy.

items.title: BreathePulse: Peripheral Guided Breathing via Implicit Airflow Cues
items.excerpt: BreathePulse is a laptop-mounted breathing guide that uses pulsed airflow as an implicit cue. In a controlled N-back study, airflow guided slower breathing most consistently during the easier task, while adding workload and producing little measurable change in stress.

items.title: EchoForce: Continuous Wearable Grip Force Estimation with Acoustic Sensing
items.excerpt: EchoForce is a wristband that estimates grip force from acoustic reflections produced by subtle skin deformation above the forearm flexor muscles. We evaluated both user-dependent and user-independent models across sessions and hand orientations.

items.title: Classifying Exoplanet Candidates from Stellar Time Series
items.excerpt: In this machine-learning course project, we represented Kepler K2 light curves using generic time-series features and compared five classifiers on a curated set of 685 stars. A random forest produced the strongest result, with an F1 score of 0.83 and cross-validated accuracy of 0.80 ± 0.06; the model ranked candidates rather than confirming new planets.
items.context: Course project, CS 4641 Machine Learning, Spring 2020

items.title: Hand Pose Estimation using Convolutional Neural Networks in Stereoscopic Vision
items.excerpt: In this computer-vision course project, we built an early-fusion convolutional model for estimating 21 hand keypoints from synchronized stereo images. The model did not converge to a usable estimator; a persistent coordinate offset made the project a practical lesson in validating camera geometry independently of end-to-end training loss.
items.context: Course project, CS 4476 Computer Vision, Fall 2020

items.title: Horizon Worlds: A Community of Practice for Social VR Design
items.excerpt: Through roughly 50 hours of participant observation and interviews with six community members, we studied how people learned, collaborated, formed roles, and handled conflict in Horizon Worlds. Its creator community operated as a community of practice, while moderation and the ephemerality of encounters shaped whether its social spaces could remain dependable.
items.context: Course project, CS 4472 Design of Online Communities, Spring 2022

items.title: ITR Atlas: Comparing Information Transfer Rates Across Interfaces
items.excerpt: The Information Transfer Rate Atlas is an independent comparison site for communication and control interfaces across HCI and BCI. We recalculate information transfer rates from original papers and system figures, providing step-by-step derivations and conservative cross-modal comparisons with tighter bounds for language and pointing tasks.

items.title: OpenRing Companion: A Local-First Health Dashboard for Tau-Ring
items.excerpt: OpenRing Companion is an independent Android companion app for Tsinghua's Tau-Ring smart ring. It replaces a data-collection-oriented interface with a local-first health dashboard that turns passive ring measurements into interpretable daily scores, trends, and intraday views while keeping health data and exports on the user's device.

items.title: Passive Haptic Learning for Accelerated Learning of Piano
items.excerpt: We developed passive haptic rehearsal: a wearable glove, light-up keyboard, and learning portal that supplement active piano practice with tactile repetition between sessions. In the primary analysis of 20 participants with complete, valid data from a 36-person in-home study, passive rehearsal increased the modeled learning rate for note accuracy by 49.7%, but did not significantly improve rhythm.

items.title: Perceived Credibility of Public Health Messages
items.excerpt: In a survey experiment with 51 Georgia Tech undergraduates, we tested whether the stated source and platform of a COVID-19 public-health message affected its credibility. Messages attributed to public-health agencies were rated above those with an unknown source; the text-only platform manipulation produced no significant effect.
items.context: Course project, PSYC 2015 Research Methods, Spring 2022

items.title: Autonomous Navigation for Mobile Robots in Open Terrain
items.excerpt: For RoboJackets' autonomous ground vehicles, I developed motor-control and path-planning software and built a full-scale Gazebo reproduction of the competition course. I later managed the mechanical, electrical, and software subteams as the project integrated perception, localization, planning, and recovery behavior into a single outdoor robot.
items.context: RoboJackets, Georgia Tech; IGVC 2019, then Jessiii after the 2020 competition was cancelled

items.title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning in the 2018 DJI RoboMaster AI Challenge
items.excerpt: I designed a recurrent reinforcement-learning and simulation framework for an autonomous robot in the 2018 DJI RoboMaster AI Challenge. Team RCMakers qualified as a finalist and placed 11th at ICRA 2018.
items.context: High-school team RCMakers; finals May 2018 at ICRA, Brisbane

items.title: Mobile Robotics for Autonomous Humanitarian Demining
items.excerpt: For the 2017 IEEE humanitarian-demining robotics challenge, our high-school team combined a low-cost mobile robot, dual-coil metal detector, decision-tree classifier, and ROS navigation stack. I worked on mine detection and supporting research; the team placed third and demonstrated the system at ICRA 2017.
items.context: High-school team RCMakers; finals May 2017 at ICRA (3rd place)

items.title: SilentSpeller: Silent Speech Text Entry using Electropalatography
items.excerpt: SilentSpeller is a hands-free text-entry system that senses tongue contact through capacitive electrodes in a dental retainer. We evaluated silent spelling with a 1,164-word vocabulary while participants were seated and walking, as well as in live text entry.

items.title: Tongue Gestures in Head Worn Devices
items.excerpt: At Microsoft Research, we collected 48,000 trials from 16 participants across eight closed-mouth tongue gestures using sensors in commercial head-worn devices. A multimodal model reached 94% accuracy, and a follow-on interaction technique used tongue gestures to confirm gaze targets without dwell for subtle, hands-free selection.

items.title: Touché: Wearable Vibrotactile Stimulation Hardware for Upper-Limb Spasticity
items.excerpt: Touché explores flexible, low-cost wearable electronics for delivering vibrotactile stimulation to people with post-stroke upper-limb spasticity. The project focuses on making extended stimulation easier to use at home and during daily activity.

items.title: AppetiteCheck: Momentary Vagus Nerve Stimulation During Eating
items.excerpt: AppetiteCheck examines momentary, non-invasive vagus nerve stimulation as a low-attention intervention during eating. In a controlled study, participants ate less and more slowly under stimulation than under sham while reporting similar post-snacking satiety.

items.title: VibroTone: Wearable Vibrotactile Stimulation for Lower-Limb Spasticity
items.excerpt: VibroTone is an adjustable wearable wrap that delivers targeted vibration to the lower leg. We investigate how stimulation location and use during rest or gait training affect muscle tone and mobility after stroke, combining measurements of spinal reflexes and muscle activity with clinical assessments.

items.title: Wardian: A Malleable Habitat for Local Agent Work
items.excerpt: Wardian is a local-first desktop habitat where work done with CLI agents becomes visible, durable, and malleable. It preserves real provider sessions, project context, coordination, and evidence, then lets repeated work become reusable prompts, skills, agent classes, and automations.

items.title: Localization of Working Memory using tfMRI
items.excerpt: In a Neuromatch Academy collaboration, we analyzed Human Connectome Project fMRI data from 100 participants across 360 cortical regions. Contrasting 2-back with 0-back tasks isolated increased frontoparietal activity and reduced activity in parts of visual cortex, but did not establish the direction of information flow between regions.

items.excerpt: Voice control provides hands-free access to computing, but there are many situations where audible speech is not appropriate. Most unvoiced speech text entry systems can not be used while on-the-go due to movement artifacts.
